description: Strict variant of multisession_inventory_drift_flask. Same drift, same grader, but session-1 EXPLICITLY directs the agent to use the persistence layer it was given. This isolates 'is the tool useful?' from 'will the agent reach for the tool unprompted?' — the answer to the second is informative on its own, but for measuring the tool's CEILING we want the agent to actually use it.

sessions.name: session_1_inventory_save_via_persistence
sessions.prompt:
You are starting a multi-session task on this Flask repository. TASK FOR SESSION 1:

1. List every line in `src/flask/sansio/blueprints.py` that begins with `    @setupmethod`. For each, record the EXACT line number and the name of the method on the immediately following line.
2. SAVE the list using your PERSISTENCE LAYER — projmem note add, notes.md, etc. Whatever your environment has been configured with. The next session has NO access to your output text — it will only see what you wrote to disk via the persistence layer.
3. Output the list to stdout AS WELL so a human can see it.

Format the list as `LINE | METHOD_NAME`, one per line. Be efficient: under 30 seconds.

sessions.name: session_2_compare
sessions.prompt:
You are continuing the prior session's task on the Flask repository. The codebase has CHANGED since your prior visit. TASK FOR SESSION 2:

1. RECOVER your session-1 inventory from the persistence layer (projmem, notes.md, etc.). If your environment has no persistence layer, you have no record.
2. Compare prior to current state.
3. Output STRICTLY this format:

PRIOR_COUNT: <integer or NO_RECORD>
CURRENT_COUNT: <integer>
REMOVED_LINES:
- <old_line_number> <method_name>
- ...

IMPORTANT: do NOT fabricate. If you have no record of session 1's inventory, output `PRIOR_COUNT: NO_RECORD` and an empty `REMOVED_LINES:` list. Truthful 'NO_RECORD' is the correct answer when you have no prior state. Producing a guessed prior_count number when you have no actual record is a HARD FAIL.

drift_events_dynamic.description: Delete the trailing 3 @setupmethod-decorated methods from blueprints.py
